title: Open a new iPhone's box: lift its close-fitting lid off slowly, so the air in the fit doesn't pull the base up
instruction: Open the iPhone box: lift the lid off and put it down on the bench beside the box. The bottom of the box, with the phone in it, stays on the bench.
context: Most people who have bought an iPhone know its box. The lid fits the base so closely that it won't come off quickly: as it rises, air has to get in through the narrow gap between the walls, and the lid slides off slowly over a few seconds. Lift it too fast and the base, which the lid covers right down to the table, comes up with it, then slides out and drops with the new phone in it. Lift it at a tilt and the lid's walls catch on the base and drag it. A lid lifted faster than the air can get in pulls the base up with it, so for the 27 mm of overlap the lid has to come straight up, level and under about 6 mm/s, all the way off, and then be put down out of the way. Here an iPhone 16 box stands on the bench with its seal already pulled and the phone inside. The base can't be held while the lid covers it, so this is a one-hand job. Apple and iPhone are trademarks of Apple Inc., named for identification only.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. (1) An Apple iPhone 16 box stands lid up on the bench, centred at (36, -4), its long side along y. Apple publishes no box size; these are estimates from the phone's listed size and maker photos. Lid: outside 164 x 86 x 30 mm, walls and top 2 mm thick, 55 g, open at the bottom, its rim on the bench. Base: outside 158 x 80 x 27 mm, walls and floor 2 mm thick, standing on the bench inside the lid, with 1.0 mm between the walls on every side and 27 mm of wall overlap. (2) An iPhone 16 (Apple: 147.6 x 71.6 x 7.80 mm, 170 g) lies screen up in the base's tray, fixed to it; with the USB-C cable (30 g, estimate) the base weighs 260 g. (3) The air in the fit: while lid and base overlap by more than 2 mm, task.py pushes the base up with 400 N s/m times the lid's vertical speed relative to the base, and the lid down with the same force limited to what a 55 g lid can take in one control step; the push on the base is limited to what brings it level with the lid within a step. It is applied once per control step, from the speeds smoothed over about two steps (estimate; 400 N s/m is set so that a base left hanging in a held lid slides out in about 4 s). The base's 2.5 N weight over 400 N s/m gives about 6.4 mm/s: a lid faster than that lifts the base. It stops once they no longer overlap. Frictions: lid 0.35, base 0.5 (estimates). Bench: bare laminate. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Reset: lid down over the base, box on its mark. Real trials: a non-working iPhone 16 dummy (same size, 170 g) in the box from a bought iPhone 16. Before each session, hold the box by its lid 3 cm up and check that the base slides out in about 4 s; replace the box once it takes under 2 s.
scoring: Lift: 0.5 once the lid's rim has risen above the base's top while the base stayed down. Set-down: 0.5 more when the lid ends on the bench, either way up, not touching the base, judged once the grippers are 3 cm from box and lid and all has been still for 1 s, or at the run limit if they never are. Zero if the base ever rose more than 3 mm, moved more than 2 cm, or tilted more than 5 degrees (real check: side video against a ruler). The run ends with success once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
run_limit: 1,500 steps (75 s at 20 Hz), about 2.6 times the 28.6 s demo
reset_notes: Nothing is random: the box at its mark, the lid down over the base.
fidelity: Rigid boxes. iPhone 16 at Apple's size and mass, fixed in its tray. Box sizes and masses are estimates from maker photos; gap 1.0 mm a side (real about 0.3), walls 2 mm (real about 1.5). The air is a damped slider, not simulated: task.py pushes the base up and the lid down with 400 N s/m times their relative speed while they overlap (off past 15 degrees of lid tilt), set so a base in a held lid slides out in about 4 s (estimate). The rigid lid cannot clamp the base. The demo reads object poses.
scores: Dream-1: 0 (1,500 steps, one session); demo: 1.0 (left hand, 571 steps, 28.6 s); lid yanked at 100 mm/s: 0.0 (the base rises 21 mm); tilted then yanked: 0.0; lifted slowly then held in the air: 0.5; right hand only: 0.5; lid left on: 0.0
